preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 10**4
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all('\n'.join(line.split()) == line for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip())
preconditions.description: Each permutation line contains exactly m space-separated integers, with no extra whitespace.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == m for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each permutation has exactly m elements, where m is given per test case.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= int(x) <= m for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each element in every permutation is an integer between 1 and m (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(line.split())) == m for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each permutation contains m distinct integers (i.e., it is a valid permutation).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 5 * 10**4 and 1 <= m <= 10 for n, m in (map(int, line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[::2]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, n (number of permutations) and m (length of each permutation) satisfy 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·10^4 and 1 ≤ m ≤ 10.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [' '.join(map(str, [max(max(k for k in range(1, m + 1) if all((a_i * a_j)[l] == l + 1 for l in range(k))) for a_j in a_perms]) for a_i in a_perms])) for a_perms in test_cases]
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output consists of n integers. The i-th integer is the largest beauty k of the permutation product a_i · a_j for any j (1 ≤ j ≤ n), where beauty is defined as the largest k such that the first k elements of the product permutation are 1, 2, ..., k.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line.split()) == n for output_line in stdout.strip().split('\n'))
postconditions.description: The output for each test case contains exactly n integers, one for each permutation in the test case.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(x) <= m for x in stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a valid beauty value (0 ≤ beauty ≤ m).
